item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Interesting entry. I personally really enjoy it in its current state, and considering the lengthy revisions and adjustments that have been happening to it for about 10 years, i assume i'm at least not entirely alone. This article is a nice piece of SCP history, considering its probably far more well known than its rating implies. I'm not entirely sure why so many people vocally dislike this piece, or try and point it out as exceptionally poorly done. Historically, keeping some aspects of an scp in the dark goes over rather well with audiences, but this seems to be an exception. And while the high number of reactions and expunges in this piece do leave a LOT to the imagination, its still a fun concept. Secure, Contain, Protect. Not Explain, Analyze, Objectify. Are there better SCPs with similar concepts, absolutely. But this one has stuck around for much longer than most in one form or another, so make of that what you will.

item.content:encoded:
I like this version more than any I've read over the years, enough to +1.

But in all rewrites, I keep getting hung up on the same detail. Based on comment history, I'm not the only one. Why for the love of jeebus and all the little fishies do they want to keep the door open?
It just makes no sense. I get that we are supposed to infer Big Scary Consequences, that an open path to hell is the least-bad option; but the redaction covers up any possible starting point to hang your imagination on.
There isn't even anything to imply how The Foundation came to the "open or else" conclusion in-universe. As far as we can see, there never has been a closure. So what are they basing the "threat to major population centers" on? Only thing I can think is that cult-leader/aircraft-engineer Blackbox from the interview left some notes behind. But that is almost purely speculation on my part.

Seeing as the last addendum conflicted with the rest of the article in terms of open/close of the door for the past three years, I tweaked it.
Specifically, the last addendum stated that people wanted to "close [it]" and "keep [it] closed", whereas the rest of the article states that closure of the door causes metric shittons of problems and you want to keep it open. These appear to be leftovers from an earlier vision; looking through the history (somewhere around versions 39 or 38 or whatever), it appears that originally the door would open and they had to close it mid-flight.
So I edited it to be "keep [it] open" in both uses in that last addendum. If this is an issue, PM me, because I'm bad at checking comment sections.

The reason why the plane needs to be in the air is this:

The speed at which SCP-616-1 closes is highly dependent on SCP-616's altitude, velocity, and [DATA EXPUNGED].

If it were on the ground when the door opened then it would close far too fast for anyone to stop it.

The last interview tells us that after some period of time, in this case four hours, the effect stops and it is simply an open door again which may be closed as normal.
